# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

130

132	
133	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">

138	                    ) : (
139	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
140	                        product={product}
141	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
142	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
143	                        quantity={quantity}
144	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
145	                      />
146	                    ))}
147	                </Stack>
148	                <Stack>
149	                  <HideOnMobile>
150	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
151	                  </HideOnMobile>
152	                  <Box display={['none', 'block', 'block', 'block']}>{primaryAction}</Box>
153	                </Stack>
154	              </Flex>
155	
156	              <Box>
157	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
158	                  <Fade in={true}>

160	                      {inventoryMessage}

162	                  </Fade>
163	                )}
164	              </Box>
165	
166	              {secondaryActions}

172	          </Box>
173	        </Stack>
174	      </ItemVariantProvider>
175	    </Box>
176	  );

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff beyond the TypeScript annotations below and a temporary
12	 * `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed). The
13	 * `<Box width="84px" backgroundColor="gray.100" {...props}>`
14	 * defaults-then-spread prop order is preserved exactly, unchanged from base — that ordering is
15	 * what lets a caller-supplied width (e.g. product-item/index.tsx's `width={['88px', '136px']}`)
16	 * override the default.
17	 *
18	 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
19	 */
20	import React from 'react';
21	import { AspectRatio, Box, Badge, Image } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
22	import { useItemVariant } from '.';
23	import { FormattedMessage } from 'react-intl';
24	import { findImageGroupBy } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils';
25	
26	// See index.tsx's own note on why this is `any` rather than a structural type.
27	type SfccVariant = any;
28	
29	type ItemImageProps = {
30	  imageProps?: Record<string, any>;
31	  ratio?: number;
32	} & Record<string, any>;
33	
34	/**
35	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
36	 * main image.
37	 *
38	 * @todo = This component will render a `SALE` badge when the qualifier is available
39	 * on the custom property `c_isSale`. This will need to be expanded upon to handle
40	 * different badge/qualifiers and property names.
41	 */
42	const ItemImage = ({ imageProps, ratio = 1, ...props }: ItemImageProps) => {
43	  const variant: SfccVariant = useItemVariant();
44	
45	  // We find the 'small' images in the variant's image groups based on variationValues and pick the first one
46	  const image = findImageGroupBy(variant?.imageGroups, {
47	    viewType: 'small',
48	    selectedVariationAttributes: variant?.variationValues,
49	  })?.images?.[0];
50	
51	  return (
52	    <Box width="84px" backgroundColor="gray.100" {...props}>
53	      <AspectRatio ratio={ratio}>
54	        <Box position="relative">
55	          {variant.c_isSale && (
56	            <Badge
57	              position="absolute"
58	              top={0}
59	              left={0}
60	              marginLeft={2}
61	              marginTop={2}
62	              fontSize="10px"
63	              variant="solid"
64	              colorScheme="blue"
65	            >
66	              <FormattedMessage
67	                defaultMessage="Sale"
68	                id="item_image.label.sale"
69	                description="A sale badge placed on top of a product image"
70	              />
71	            </Badge>
72	          )}
73	          {variant.isProductUnavailable && (
74	            <Badge
75	              position="absolute"
76	              top={0}
77	              left={0}
78	              marginLeft={2}
79	              marginTop={2}
80	              fontSize="10px"
81	              variant="solid"
82	              colorScheme="red"
83	            >
84	              <FormattedMessage
85	                defaultMessage="Unavailable"
86	                id="item_image.label.unavailable"
87	                description="A unavailable badge placed on top of a product image"
88	              />
89	            </Badge>
90	          )}
91	
92	          {image && (
93	            <Image alt={image.alt} src={`${image.disBaseLink || image.link}`} ignoreFallback={true} {...imageProps} />
94	          )}
95	        </Box>
96	      </AspectRatio>
97	    </Box>
98	  );
99	};
100	
101	export default ItemImage;

import { FONT_MEDIUM, FONT_REGULAR, FONT_SERIF } from './fonts';
import { colors } from './colour';
import { fontSizes, lineHeights, letterSpacings, fontWeights } from './typography';
import { spacing, borderWidths, focusRingOffsets } from './spacing';
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, megaMenuSizes } from './sizes';
import { grid } from './gridSystem';
import { motion } from './motion';

  '--zimm-color-grey-300': colors.grey[300],
  '--zimm-color-grey-200': colors.grey[200],
  '--zimm-color-grey-100': colors.grey[100],
  '--zimm-color-grey-white': colors.grey.white,

  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Ivory ----

  '--zimm-color-ivory-300': colors.ivory[300],
  '--zimm-color-ivory-200': colors.ivory[200],
  '--zimm-color-ivory-100': colors.ivory[100],

  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Status ----

  '--zimm-color-orange-500': colors.orange[500],
  '--zimm-color-red-500': colors.red[500],

  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Opacity (base: grey/900) ----
  '--zimm-color-opacity-50': colors.opacity[50],
  '--zimm-color-opacity-40': colors.opacity[40],
  '--zimm-color-opacity-30': colors.opacity[30],
  '--zimm-color-opacity-15': colors.opacity[15],

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Text ----

  // ---- Spacing: numeric aliases ----
  // Ported from the Handover's numeric spacing scale. The ones below that coincide
  // with a named-scale step reference it directly; the rest have no foundation-file
  // source to derive from (not duplicates — genuinely distinct Handover values), so

  '--zimm-scale-025': '1px',
  '--zimm-scale-200': spacing.xs, // 8px

  '--zimm-scale-700': '28px',

  '--zimm-grid-margin-mobile': grid.containerPadding.base,

  // Outer container cap — shared by header/footer/main content. 'none' today; see

  '--zimm-grid-max-width': grid.maxWidth,

  // ---- Spacing: Action sizing ----

  '--zimm-size-action-gap': actionSizes.gap,

  // ---- Border widths ----

  // ---- Icon sizes ----
  '--zimm-icon-size-xl': iconSizes.xl,
  '--zimm-icon-size-lg': iconSizes.lg,
  '--zimm-icon-size-md': iconSizes.md,
  '--zimm-icon-size-sm': iconSizes.sm,

  // ---- Mega menu sizing ----
  '--zimm-size-mega-menu-two-column-max-width': megaMenuSizes.twoColumnMaxWidth,

  // ---- Motion (PROVISIONAL — pending formal sign-off, see motion.ts) ----
  '--zimm-motion-duration-fast': motion.duration.fast,
  '--zimm-motion-duration-default': motion.duration.default,
  '--zimm-motion-duration-slow': motion.duration.slow,

  '--zimm-motion-easing-slides': motion.easing.slides,
  '--zimm-motion-easing-fades': motion.easing.fades,
};

content.content:
1	# PRD – Gift Cards & Credit Notes
2	
3	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheet "Gift Cards & Credit Notes" (GC). Last updated: 2026-06-07.*
4	
5	*All GC requirements are **Confirmed** (signed off 2026-05-12 by Emma, Rebecca; sign-off date 2026-06-01). GC-049 max-cards limit remains open (see §12).*
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Scope
10	
11	Gift cards and credit notes are available on **domestic storefronts only** (AU, UK, EU, US). Not available on Global-e international storefronts (HK, ME, US Int, EU Int) at launch — international gift card support is on the future roadmap (GC-050).
12	
13	Two types:
14	- **Physical gift card** — delivered by post
15	- **Digital gift card** — delivered by email on a scheduled date
16	
17	Both types are processed by **GiveX**. Both types are tax-exempt across all storefronts (GC-020).
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. Gift Card PDP (GC-001 – GC-008)
22	
23	- Customer selects an amount from **fixed denominations: $100, $200, $250, $300, $500** via a searchable dropdown — applies to both physical (GC-001, GC-002) and digital (GC-003, GC-004) gift cards
24	- Customer enters: sender name, recipient name, recipient email address, delivery date, and optional personal message (GC-001, GC-003)
25	- **Delivery date picker**: calendar with month navigation; restricted to within 3 months from today; future dates beyond 3 months are greyed out (GC-005, GC-006)
26	- Recipient email is validated for format before Add to Bag is enabled (GC-007)
27	- Sender and recipient may be the same person (GC-008)
28	
29	---
30	
31	## 3. Mini-Cart (GC-009 – GC-010)
32	
33	- Gift card displayed in mini-cart: gift card image, price, quantity only (GC-009)
34	- Actions: **Move to Wishlist (physical cards only)**, Remove (GC-010)
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 4. Cart Page
39	
40	### Digital gift card (GC-011 – GC-015)
41	- Displayed in cart: gift card image, price, quantity, sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, and personal message (GC-011)
42	- Customer can adjust quantity (GC-012)
43	- Actions: **Edit** (digital only), Move to Wishlist, Remove (GC-013)
44	- Selecting Edit navigates back to the Gift Card PDP with all previously entered details pre-populated (GC-014)
45	- CTA changes to **"Update Bag"** instead of "Add to Bag" when editing (GC-015)
46	
47	### Physical gift card (GC-016 – GC-018)
48	- Displayed in cart: gift card image, price, quantity (GC-016)
49	- Customer can adjust quantity (GC-017)
50	- Actions: Move to Wishlist, Remove — no Edit action for physical gift card (GC-018)
51	
52	### Both types (GC-019 – GC-021)
53	- Default maximum 3 units per size applies across all SKUs, including gift cards (GC-019). Note: ability to override the default max at SKU level via a configurable product attribute requires a custom build and is not OOTB in SFCC — logged as enhancement.
54	- Both physical and digital gift cards can be in the same order (GC-021)
55	
56	---
57	
58	## 5. Checkout
59	
60	### Order Summary (GC-022)
61	- Gift card displayed in the checkout order summary showing gift card image, price, and quantity (GC-022)
62	
63	### Digital gift card only (GC-023 – GC-024)
64	- **Bypasses shipping address and delivery method steps** — proceeds directly to payment (GC-023)
65	- Collect from Boutique option suppressed (GC-024)
66	
67	### Digital gift card + physical product (GC-025 – GC-026)
68	- Standard checkout flow including shipping address and delivery method (GC-025)
69	- Collect from Boutique option suppressed regardless of other product eligibility (GC-026)
70	
71	### Physical gift card only (GC-027 – GC-028)
72	- Standard checkout flow including shipping and delivery (GC-027)
73	- Collect from Boutique is **not** restricted for physical gift cards (GC-028)
74	
75	### Physical gift card + other product (GC-029 – GC-030)
76	- Standard checkout flow (GC-029)
77	- Collect from Boutique is **not** restricted (GC-030)
78	
79	### Payment restriction (GC-031)
80	- Gift card payment method is hidden at checkout if a physical or digital gift card is already in the cart (GC-031)
81	- *(This is confirmed also in PAY-011a/b in checkout.md)*
82	
83	---
84	
85	## 6. Order Confirmation
86	
87	- Domestic orders: order confirmation via Narvar (GC-032)
88	- International orders: order confirmation via Global-e (GC-033)
89	
90	---
91	
92	## 7. Redeeming Gift Cards & Credit Notes at Checkout (GC-034 – GC-049)
93	
94	### Entry & validation
95	- Gift card payment tab shows: card number field + PIN field (GC-034)
96	- Both card number and PIN required before applying (GC-035)
97	- Credit notes use the same card number + PIN mechanism — no distinction from gift cards (GC-036)
98	- **Check Balance** link at the gift card entry field allows customer to verify balance before applying (GC-037)
99	- Instructional text prompts customer to click Apply after entering each card (GC-038)
100	- Real-time validation against **GiveX** on Apply; returns available balance and applies it against order total (GC-039)
101	- Customer can remove an applied gift card or credit note and revert to another payment method (GC-040)
102	- Any gift card/credit note with a remaining balance greater than zero is accepted (GC-041)
103	
104	### Error states
105	- Invalid card or insufficient funds in storefront currency: error displayed (e.g. "Invalid card. Card must have sufficient AUD funds.") (GC-042)
106	- GiveX unavailable: error displayed; gift card/credit note payment blocked until GiveX is available (GC-043). "Unavailable" means the redemption path (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX, per §11) has returned an error after exhausting any failover/retry — the PWA does not see individual GiveX call failures.
107	
108	### Payment combinations (GC-044 – GC-049)
109	- Gift card/credit note as the **sole payment method** — full order total applied against the balance via GiveX (GC-044)
110	- Gift card/credit note + credit card, PayPal, or Apple Pay — gift card/credit note applied first; remaining balance charged to the second method (GC-045)
111	- Gift card + credit note — can be combined (GC-046)
112	- Gift card/credit note + Retail Rewards vouchers — can be combined (GC-047)
113	- Gift card/credit note + promotional codes — can be combined (GC-048)
114	- **Multiple gift cards/credit notes in a single transaction** — supported; maximum limit open (Zimmermann to confirm if there is a max — GC-049 Open)
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 8. Global-e International (GC-050)
119	
120	- Gift card and credit note redemption is **not supported** on Global-e international storefronts at launch (GC-050)
121	- Future roadmap item to include gift cards in Global-e orders
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 9. My Account — Balance Check (GC-051 – GC-062)
126	
127	Available on **all storefronts** (domestic and international).
128	
129	### Layout & flow
130	- Gift Cards / Credit Notes section displayed within My Account, accessible from the left-hand navigation (GC-051)
131	- Input field allows the customer to enter a gift card or credit note number to check the balance (GC-052)
132	- Same input field is used for both gift card and credit note balance checks — no distinction between the two (GC-057)
133	- On **Submit**, the system retrieves the balance from GiveX via a real-time API call (GC-053)
134	- Result displays: card/note number, current available balance, and expiry date returned from GiveX (GC-054)
135	- Customer can check another gift card or credit note without leaving the page (GC-055)
136	- Balance check result is displayed for one card or credit note at a time (GC-058)
137	
138	### Validation & access
139	- No inline validation on the input field before submitting to GiveX — the API call is made regardless and any error returned by GiveX is displayed to the customer (GC-056)
140	- Balance check is treated as a one-off lookup — customer is **not** required to be logged in, and the result is not saved against any account (GC-059)
141	- No per-customer cap on balance check attempts (GC-062), subject to abuse-protection controls. The MRT balance-check route applies rate-limiting and bot protection before forwarding to MuleSoft (which owns the GiveX socket, per §11) — GiveX security guidance requires WAF / bot management / rate-limit / CAPTCHA in front of the unauthenticated balance-check endpoint, since the credential is merchant-level rather than per-shopper
142	
143	### Error states
144	- Appropriate error message displayed if a gift card or credit note has expired or has a zero balance (GC-060)
145	- Error message displayed if GiveX is unavailable at the point of submission (GC-061)
146	
147	*(Cross-reference: account.md section 6 — balance check entry point in My Account navigation.)*
148	
149	---
150	
151	## 10. Security & Handling of Card Numbers
152	
153	Gift card numbers and PINs are treated as payment credentials (per *GIVEX Numbers Defined.pdf*: a GiveX card is `[prefix][serial][check]`, only the **serial portion** may be displayed or logged). For PWA work this means:
154	
155	- **Transport.** Card number and PIN must be sent in the request **body** (POST), never as a query string. URLs end up in MRT access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
156	- **Storage.** No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookie may hold the full card number or PIN. Form state lives in React only and is cleared on unmount.
157	- **Logging.** No `console.log`, no Sentry breadcrumb / `beforeSend` capture, no GTM dataLayer push, no analytics event may contain the full card number or PIN. Add a redaction filter in the logger and a Sentry scrubber for the gift-card payload. Do not enable body-logging middleware on the MRT balance-check route.
158	- **Display.** After submission, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). The applied-gift-cards list in cart/checkout stores the masked form returned by SFCC — never echo back the original input.
159	- **Server-side.** MRT forwards the payload to MuleSoft — which owns the GiveX socket for both balance check (MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX) and redemption (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX) — and returns only the masked response to the browser, see §11. The full PAN does not appear in any MRT log, response body, or persisted store. The unmasked-PAN boundary sits with MuleSoft/GiveX, not the PWA.
160	
161	(Cross-reference: [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../.claude/rules/conventions.md) — Logging.)
162	
163	---
164	
165	## 11. Architecture Note — PWA ↔ GiveX
166	
167	Two distinct integration paths. The Third-Party Integrations row describes balance check as a *"direct MRT API connection"* and redemption as *"via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft"*. Confirmed with Integration: *"direct MRT"* means **MRT-initiated** (not via SFCC) — **MuleSoft remains the upstream for balance check**, because GiveX is reachable only over a persistent socket the MRT runtime cannot hold.
168	
169	- **Balance check (My Account, GC-051–062; Check Balance link, GC-037).** PWA → MRT → **MuleSoft** → GiveX. GiveX exposes only a persistent TCP socket (JSON-RPC/XML-RPC) that the MRT Workers runtime cannot hold, so MuleSoft owns the GiveX socket pool, primary/secondary host failover, and credentials. MRT exposes an HTTPS endpoint, applies rate-limit / bot protection in front of the unauthenticated balance-check route (see §9, GC-062), and holds the MuleSoft credential as an env var.
170	- **Checkout redemption (GC-034–049).** Gift card and credit note redemption is handled **via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft**. Real-time validation on Apply (GC-039) and the resulting payment-instrument state (masked number, applied amount, remaining balance) flow back to the PWA through that path. The PWA does not hold any GiveX socket itself.
171	- **Reversal on capture failure.** If GiveX redemption succeeds but downstream card capture (Adyen) fails, reversal/cancel is handled by the redemption path (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX), not the PWA.
172	
173	PWA-side blockers before live wiring is possible:
174	- GiveX balance-check API contract for the MuleSoft connection (request/response schema, error taxonomy mapping to GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061).
175	- GiveX endpoint URLs and credential per environment (dev / UAT / prod).
176	- Redemption payload/response shape exposed through the NewStore adaptor / MuleSoft for cart/checkout.
177	
178	Until those are published, balance-check work proceeds against a typed mock; checkout redemption work waits on the redemption contract.
179	
180	---
181	
182	## 12. Open Items
183	
184	- Maximum number of gift cards/credit notes per transaction — Zimmermann to confirm (GC-049)
185	- Gift card fraud review hold — Zimmermann would like to review the hold process to enable digital GC code delivery sooner (PAY-044)

# PRD – Gift Cards & Credit Notes

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheet "Gift Cards & Credit Notes" (GC). Last updated: 2026-06-07.*

*All GC requirements are **Confirmed** (signed off 2026-05-12 by Emma, Rebecca; sign-off date 2026-06-01). GC-049 max-cards limit remains open (see §12).*

---

## 1. Scope

Gift cards and credit notes are available on **domestic storefronts only** (AU, UK, EU, US). Not available on Global-e international storefronts (HK, ME, US Int, EU Int) at launch — international gift card support is on the future roadmap (GC-050).

Two types:
- **Physical gift card** — delivered by post
- **Digital gift card** — delivered by email on a scheduled date

Both types are processed by **GiveX**. Both types are tax-exempt across all storefronts (GC-020).

---

## 2. Gift Card PDP (GC-001 – GC-008)

- Customer selects an amount from **fixed denominations: $100, $200, $250, $300, $500** via a searchable dropdown — applies to both physical (GC-001, GC-002) and digital (GC-003, GC-004) gift cards
- Customer enters: sender name, recipient name, recipient email address, delivery date, and optional personal message (GC-001, GC-003)
- **Delivery date picker**: calendar with month navigation; restricted to within 3 months from today; future dates beyond 3 months are greyed out (GC-005, GC-006)
- Recipient email is validated for format before Add to Bag is enabled (GC-007)
- Sender and recipient may be the same person (GC-008)

---

## 3. Mini-Cart (GC-009 – GC-010)

- Gift card displayed in mini-cart: gift card image, price, quantity only (GC-009)
- Actions: **Move to Wishlist (physical cards only)**, Remove (GC-010)

---

## 4. Cart Page

### Digital gift card (GC-011 – GC-015)
- Displayed in cart: gift card image, price, quantity, sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, and personal message (GC-011)
- Customer can adjust quantity (GC-012)
- Actions: **Edit** (digital only), Move to Wishlist, Remove (GC-013)
- Selecting Edit navigates back to the Gift Card PDP with all previously entered details pre-populated (GC-014)
- CTA changes to **"Update Bag"** instead of "Add to Bag" when editing (GC-015)

### Physical gift card (GC-016 – GC-018)
- Displayed in cart: gift card image, price, quantity (GC-016)
- Customer can adjust quantity (GC-017)
- Actions: Move to Wishlist, Remove — no Edit action for physical gift card (GC-018)

### Both types (GC-019 – GC-021)
- Default maximum 3 units per size applies across all SKUs, including gift cards (GC-019). Note: ability to override the default max at SKU level via a configurable product attribute requires a custom build and is not OOTB in SFCC — logged as enhancement.
- Both physical and digital gift cards can be in the same order (GC-021)

---

## 5. Checkout

### Order Summary (GC-022)
- Gift card displayed in the checkout order summary showing gift card image, price, and quantity (GC-022)

### Digital gift card only (GC-023 – GC-024)
- **Bypasses shipping address and delivery method steps** — proceeds directly to payment (GC-023)
- Collect from Boutique option suppressed (GC-024)

### Digital gift card + physical product (GC-025 – GC-026)
- Standard checkout flow including shipping address and delivery method (GC-025)
- Collect from Boutique option suppressed regardless of other product eligibility (GC-026)

### Physical gift card only (GC-027 – GC-028)
- Standard checkout flow including shipping and delivery (GC-027)
- Collect from Boutique is **not** restricted for physical gift cards (GC-028)

### Physical gift card + other product (GC-029 – GC-030)
- Standard checkout flow (GC-029)
- Collect from Boutique is **not** restricted (GC-030)

### Payment restriction (GC-031)
- Gift card payment method is hidden at checkout if a physical or digital gift card is already in the cart (GC-031)
- *(This is confirmed also in PAY-011a/b in checkout.md)*

---

## 6. Order Confirmation

- Domestic orders: order confirmation via Narvar (GC-032)
- International orders: order confirmation via Global-e (GC-033)

---

## 7. Redeeming Gift Cards & Credit Notes at Checkout (GC-034 – GC-049)

### Entry & validation
- Gift card payment tab shows: card number field + PIN field (GC-034)
- Both card number and PIN required before applying (GC-035)
- Credit notes use the same card number + PIN mechanism — no distinction from gift cards (GC-036)
- **Check Balance** link at the gift card entry field allows customer to verify balance before applying (GC-037)
- Instructional text prompts customer to click Apply after entering each card (GC-038)
- Real-time validation against **GiveX** on Apply; returns available balance and applies it against order total (GC-039)
- Customer can remove an applied gift card or credit note and revert to another payment method (GC-040)
- Any gift card/credit note with a remaining balance greater than zero is accepted (GC-041)

### Error states
- Invalid card or insufficient funds in storefront currency: error displayed (e.g. "Invalid card. Card must have sufficient AUD funds.") (GC-042)
- GiveX unavailable: error displayed; gift card/credit note payment blocked until GiveX is available (GC-043). "Unavailable" means the redemption path (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX, per §11) has returned an error after exhausting any failover/retry — the PWA does not see individual GiveX call failures.

### Payment combinations (GC-044 – GC-049)
- Gift card/credit note as the **sole payment method** — full order total applied against the balance via GiveX (GC-044)
- Gift card/credit note + credit card, PayPal, or Apple Pay — gift card/credit note applied first; remaining balance charged to the second method (GC-045)
- Gift card + credit note — can be combined (GC-046)
- Gift card/credit note + Retail Rewards vouchers — can be combined (GC-047)
- Gift card/credit note + promotional codes — can be combined (GC-048)
- **Multiple gift cards/credit notes in a single transaction** — supported; maximum limit open (Zimmermann to confirm if there is a max — GC-049 Open)

---

## 8. Global-e International (GC-050)

- Gift card and credit note redemption is **not supported** on Global-e international storefronts at launch (GC-050)
- Future roadmap item to include gift cards in Global-e orders

---

## 9. My Account — Balance Check (GC-051 – GC-062)

Available on **all storefronts** (domestic and international).

### Layout & flow
- Gift Cards / Credit Notes section displayed within My Account, accessible from the left-hand navigation (GC-051)
- Input field allows the customer to enter a gift card or credit note number to check the balance (GC-052)
- Same input field is used for both gift card and credit note balance checks — no distinction between the two (GC-057)
- On **Submit**, the system retrieves the balance from GiveX via a real-time API call (GC-053)
- Result displays: card/note number, current available balance, and expiry date returned from GiveX (GC-054)
- Customer can check another gift card or credit note without leaving the page (GC-055)
- Balance check result is displayed for one card or credit note at a time (GC-058)

### Validation & access
- No inline validation on the input field before submitting to GiveX — the API call is made regardless and any error returned by GiveX is displayed to the customer (GC-056)
- Balance check is treated as a one-off lookup — customer is **not** required to be logged in, and the result is not saved against any account (GC-059)
- No per-customer cap on balance check attempts (GC-062), subject to abuse-protection controls. The MRT balance-check route applies rate-limiting and bot protection before forwarding to MuleSoft (which owns the GiveX socket, per §11) — GiveX security guidance requires WAF / bot management / rate-limit / CAPTCHA in front of the unauthenticated balance-check endpoint, since the credential is merchant-level rather than per-shopper

### Error states
- Appropriate error message displayed if a gift card or credit note has expired or has a zero balance (GC-060)
- Error message displayed if GiveX is unavailable at the point of submission (GC-061)

*(Cross-reference: account.md section 6 — balance check entry point in My Account navigation.)*

---

## 10. Security & Handling of Card Numbers

Gift card numbers and PINs are treated as payment credentials (per *GIVEX Numbers Defined.pdf*: a GiveX card is `[prefix][serial][check]`, only the **serial portion** may be displayed or logged). For PWA work this means:

- **Transport.** Card number and PIN must be sent in the request **body** (POST), never as a query string. URLs end up in MRT access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
- **Storage.** No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookie may hold the full card number or PIN. Form state lives in React only and is cleared on unmount.
- **Logging.** No `console.log`, no Sentry breadcrumb / `beforeSend` capture, no GTM dataLayer push, no analytics event may contain the full card number or PIN. Add a redaction filter in the logger and a Sentry scrubber for the gift-card payload. Do not enable body-logging middleware on the MRT balance-check route.
- **Display.** After submission, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). The applied-gift-cards list in cart/checkout stores the masked form returned by SFCC — never echo back the original input.
- **Server-side.** MRT forwards the payload to MuleSoft — which owns the GiveX socket for both balance check (MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX) and redemption (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX) — and returns only the masked response to the browser, see §11. The full PAN does not appear in any MRT log, response body, or persisted store. The unmasked-PAN boundary sits with MuleSoft/GiveX, not the PWA.

(Cross-reference: [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../.claude/rules/conventions.md) — Logging.)

---

## 11. Architecture Note — PWA ↔ GiveX

Two distinct integration paths. The Third-Party Integrations row describes balance check as a *"direct MRT API connection"* and redemption as *"via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft"*. Confirmed with Integration: *"direct MRT"* means **MRT-initiated** (not via SFCC) — **MuleSoft remains the upstream for balance check**, because GiveX is reachable only over a persistent socket the MRT runtime cannot hold.

- **Balance check (My Account, GC-051–062; Check Balance link, GC-037).** PWA → MRT → **MuleSoft** → GiveX. GiveX exposes only a persistent TCP socket (JSON-RPC/XML-RPC) that the MRT Workers runtime cannot hold, so MuleSoft owns the GiveX socket pool, primary/secondary host failover, and credentials. MRT exposes an HTTPS endpoint, applies rate-limit / bot protection in front of the unauthenticated balance-check route (see §9, GC-062), and holds the MuleSoft credential as an env var.
- **Checkout redemption (GC-034–049).** Gift card and credit note redemption is handled **via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft**. Real-time validation on Apply (GC-039) and the resulting payment-instrument state (masked number, applied amount, remaining balance) flow back to the PWA through that path. The PWA does not hold any GiveX socket itself.
- **Reversal on capture failure.** If GiveX redemption succeeds but downstream card capture (Adyen) fails, reversal/cancel is handled by the redemption path (NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX), not the PWA.

PWA-side blockers before live wiring is possible:
- GiveX balance-check API contract for the MuleSoft connection (request/response schema, error taxonomy mapping to GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061).
- GiveX endpoint URLs and credential per environment (dev / UAT / prod).
- Redemption payload/response shape exposed through the NewStore adaptor / MuleSoft for cart/checkout.

Until those are published, balance-check work proceeds against a typed mock; checkout redemption work waits on the redemption contract.

---

## 12. Open Items

- Maximum number of gift cards/credit notes per transaction — Zimmermann to confirm (GC-049)
- Gift card fraud review hold — Zimmermann would like to review the hold process to enable digital GC code delivery sooner (PAY-044)

8	import React from 'react'
9	import PropTypes from 'prop-types'
10	import {Box} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
11	import CurrentPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/current-price'
12	import ListPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/list-price'
13	
14	/**
15	 * @param priceData - price info extracted from a product
16	 * // If a product is a set,
17	 *      on PLP, Show From X where X is the lowest of its children
18	 *      on PDP, Show From X where X is the lowest of its children and
19	 *          the set children will have it own price as From X (cross) Y
20	 * // if a product is a master
21	 *      on PLP and PDP, show From X (cross) Y , the X and Y are
22	 *          current and list price of variant that has the lowest price (including promotionalPrice)
23	 * // if a standard/bundle
24	 *      show exact price on PLP and PDP as X (cross) Y
25	 * @param currency - currency
26	 * @param quantity - quantity to take into the account for price display
27	 * @param currentPriceProps - extra props to be passing to CurrentPrice component
28	 * @param listPriceProps - extra props to be passing to ListPrice component
29	 * @param labelForA11y - label to be used for a11y
30	 */
31	const DisplayPrice = ({
32	    labelForA11y,
33	    priceData,
34	    currency,
35	    quantity = 1,
36	    currentPriceProps = {},
37	    listPriceProps = {}
38	}) => {
39	    const {listPrice, currentPrice, isASet, isMaster, isOnSale, isRange} = priceData
40	    const renderCurrentPrice = (isRange) => (
41	        <CurrentPrice
42	            labelForA11y={labelForA11y}
43	            price={currentPrice * quantity}
44	            as="b"
45	            currency={currency}
46	            isRange={isRange}
47	            {...currentPriceProps}
48	        />
49	    )
50	
51	    const renderListPrice = (isRange) =>
52	        listPrice && (
53	            <ListPrice
54	                labelForA11y={labelForA11y}
55	                currency={currency}
56	                price={listPrice * quantity}
57	                isRange={isRange}
58	                {...listPriceProps}
59	            />
60	        )
61	
62	    const renderPriceSet = (isRange) => (
63	        <>
64	            {renderCurrentPrice(isRange)} {isOnSale && renderListPrice(isRange)}
65	        </>
66	    )
67	
68	    if (isASet) {
69	        return renderCurrentPrice(true)
70	    }
71	
72	    if (isMaster) {
73	        return renderPriceSet(isRange)
74	    }
75	
76	    return <Box>{renderPriceSet(false)}</Box>
77	}
78	
79	DisplayPrice.propTypes = {
80	    priceData: PropTypes.shape({
81	        currentPrice: PropTypes.number.isRequired,
82	        isOnSale: PropTypes.bool.isRequired,
83	        listPrice: PropTypes.number,
84	        pricePerUnit: PropTypes.number,
85	        isASet: PropTypes.bool,
86	        isMaster: PropTypes.bool,
87	        isRange: PropTypes.bool,
88	        maxPrice: PropTypes.number,
89	        tieredPrice: PropTypes.number
90	    }),
91	    currency: PropTypes.string.isRequired,
92	    labelForA11y: PropTypes.string,
93	    currentPriceProps: PropTypes.object,
94	    listPriceProps: PropTypes.object,
95	    quantity: PropTypes.number
96	}
97	
98	export default DisplayPrice

246	// `textStyle` sets fontFamily/fontWeight/lineHeight/letterSpacing/textTransform via
247	// Chakra's expansion pass. BUT extendTheme deep-merges our sizes with Chakra's built-in
248	// Button sizes, and Chakra's default lg has `fontSize: 'lg'` (1.125rem = 18px) and sm
249	// has `fontSize: 'sm'` (0.875rem = 14px). Because direct CSS props applied after the
250	// textStyle expansion win in Chakra's style pipeline, the merged `fontSize` from Chakra's
251	// default overrides the textStyle-derived value. Fix: set `fontSize` explicitly here using
252	// the zimm CSS var so it overwrites the leaked default and the final rendered size matches

264	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)', // 500
265	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs)', // 16px
266	    textStyle: 'button',
267	  },
268	  sm: {

270	    px: 'var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-md)', // 20px — confirmed by Figma 901:2897
271	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)', // 12px
272	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)', // 500
273	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)', // 18px
274	    textStyle: 'buttonSm',
275	  },

277	  // breakpoint, but horizontal padding is 32px at every breakpoint — NOT responsive.
278	  // Corrected 2026-09: the previous version of this comment claimed padding also stepped
279	  // down to 20px on mobile ("Figma confirms all three variants"); live Figma inspection
280	  // showed that was wrong — px was always meant to be var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg).
281	  // Mobile: 40px h, 32px px, buttonSm (12px/500/18px lh)
282	  // Desktop (md+): 52px h, 32px px, button (14px/500/16px lh)
283	  // Also used by primary/secondary buttons inside the auth drawer (size="adaptive")
284	  // via ZimmButton's adaptive→social size mapping — same tokens, different variant colours.
285	  social: {

287	    // align-items:center always has space to distribute. minH alone can resolve to nothing

289	    // centering space. whiteSpace:normal (from the social variant) still allows text wrapping

296	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)',
297	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)',
298	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)',
299	    textStyle: 'buttonSm',

302	      fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)',

309	  //

312	  // previous `p: 'xs'` read as a 32px target and rendered 16x16 — the icon's own boxSize.

314	  // var, not 'xl': min-width/height resolve through theme.sizes (xl = 36rem = 576px), not
315	  // theme.space. Same rule and same token as clearButton in zimmTextInput.ts, which is the
316	  // sibling control in the same trailing slot.

319	    minW: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',

321	  },

* Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-name.jsx
 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step beyond the TypeScript annotation and a
 * temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed).
 *
 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
 * `Link` is not overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing at time of
 * writing), so it stays on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path.
 *
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2), bug fix: base had `<Link {...props} color="black.600" to={...}>` —
 * spreading `props` BEFORE the explicit `color`/`to`, the opposite order from item-image/
 * item-attributes/item-price's own `{...props}` placement (spread last), so a caller-supplied
 * `color` was silently overridden here instead of taking precedence, unlike those three
 * siblings. Fixed by moving `color` ahead of the spread, matching the siblings' order — `to`
 * stays after the spread, unchanged, since it is data-derived (from `productId`) and was never
 * meant to be caller-overridable the way `color` is. No current base caller passes `color`, so
 * nothing observable changes for them; this only matters going forward.
 *
 * Also restyled per the Figma cart-item spec: `fontSize="md"` (a bare Chakra token — this
 * repo's own `fontSizes` scale is deliberately NOT registered as `theme.fontSizes`, see
 * typography.ts, so that literal was silently reading Chakra's own unrelated default) replaced
 * by `textStyle="productNames"`, which also carries the spec's "uppercase" requirement (see
 * typography.ts's `productNames` entry). The bug-fixed default colour is expressed as a literal
 * `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` prop rather than routed through the recipe: a plain literal
 * prop is provably override-safe here regardless of `Link`'s own internal implementation (it
 * lands in the same `props` bucket a caller's own `color` would use), where `__css`/`sx` on this
 * specific base `Link` wrapper is not — see item-variant.css.ts's own docblock for the
 * `__css`-discarding hazard that rules `__css` out for a plain Chakra `Text`, a nearby but
 * distinct case worth being equally careful about here.
 */
import React from 'react';
import { useItemVariant } from '.';
import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
import { Heading } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

/**
 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this components simply renders
 * the item's name using the cart item field `productName`. We use this field
 * rather than variant `name` field as the variant detail may not yet be
 * available upon rendering.
 */
const ItemName = (props: Record<string, any>) => {
  const variant = useItemVariant();
  const productId = variant?.master?.masterId || variant.id;

  return (
    <Heading as="h2" textStyle="productNames">
      <Link color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" {...props} to={`/product/${productId}`}>
        {variant.productName || variant.name}
      </Link>
    </Heading>
  );
};

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
3	import { renderHook, type RenderHookOptions } from '@testing-library/react';
4	
5	/**
6	 * Builds a fresh QueryClient per call — test isolation, no cache bleed between tests.
7	 * Matches `_app-config/index.tsx`'s real `defaultOptions` for retry/refetchOnWindowFocus so a
8	 * hook under test behaves the same as it does in the running app.
9	 */
10	const createTestQueryClient = () =>
11	  new QueryClient({
12	    defaultOptions: {
13	      queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false },
14	    },
15	  });
16	
17	/**
18	 * Renders a hook that calls `@tanstack/react-query`'s `useQuery` inside a fresh
19	 * `QueryClientProvider` — the same wrapper `_app-config`'s `withReactQuery(AppConfig, ...)`
20	 * mounts for every page in the real app, so a hook under test needs no provider of its own
21	 * beyond this. See `.claude/rules/testing.md` > Commerce SDK hooks for the equivalent
22	 * `renderWithProviders` pattern this mirrors for `CommerceApiProvider`-dependent hooks.
23	 *
24	 * @param callback the hook to render
25	 * @param options `renderHook` options other than `wrapper`, which this helper supplies
26	 * @returns the same result `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook` returns
27	 */
28	export const renderHookWithQueryClient = <TResult, TProps>(
29	  callback: (props: TProps) => TResult,
30	  options?: Omit<RenderHookOptions<TProps>, 'wrapper'>,
31	) => {
32	  const queryClient = createTestQueryClient();
33	  return renderHook(callback, {
34	    ...options,
35	    wrapper: ({ children }) => <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>,
36	  });
37	};

45	    const variant = useVariant(
46	        product,
47	        isProductPartOfSet,
48	        isProductPartOfBundle,
49	        controlledVariationValues
50	    )
51	    const isStandardProduct = product?.type?.item
52	    const variationParams = useVariationParams(
53	        product,
54	        isProductPartOfSet,
55	        isProductPartOfBundle,
56	        controlledVariationValues
57	    )
58	    const variationAttributes = useVariationAttributes(
59	        product,
60	        isProductPartOfSet,
61	        isProductPartOfBundle,
62	        controlledVariationValues,
63	        onVariationChange
64	    )
65	    const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState(initialQuantity)
66	    const {selectedStore} = useSelectedStore()
67	
68	    // A product is considered out of stock if the stock level is 0 or if we have all our
69	    // variation attributes selected, but don't have a variant. We do this because the API
70	    // will sometimes return all the variants even if they are out of stock, but for other
71	    // products it won't.
72	    const isOutOfStock =
73	        !stockLevel ||
74	        (!isProductABundle &&
75	            !variant &&
76	            !isStandardProduct &&
77	            Object.keys(variationParams).length === variationAttributes.length) ||
78	        (!isProductABundle && variant && !variant.orderable)
79	    const unfulfillable = stockLevel < quantity
80	
81	    // Product details for selected store
82	    const selectedStoreInventory = getInventoryById(product, selectedStore?.inventoryId)
83	    const selectedStoreStockLevel = selectedStoreInventory?.stockLevel || 0
84	    const selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName =
85	        selectedStoreInventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
86	    // selectedStoreStockLevel and selectedStoreInventory are already variant specific,
87	    // so we don't need to check for variation attributes
88	    const isSelectedStoreOutOfStock = !selectedStoreStockLevel || !selectedStoreInventory?.orderable
89	    const selectedStoreUnfulfillable = selectedStoreStockLevel < quantity
90	
91	    // Use appropriate inventory based on pickup/delivery selection
92	    const currentStockLevel = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreStockLevel : stockLevel
93	    const currentLowestStockLevelProductName = pickupInStore
94	        ? selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName
95	        : lowestStockLevelProductName
96	    const currentIsOutOfStock = pickupInStore ? isSelectedStoreOutOfStock : isOutOfStock
97	    const currentUnfulfillable = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreUnfulfillable : unfulfillable
98	
99	    const inventoryMessages = {
100	        [OUT_OF_STOCK]: intl.formatMessage({
101	            defaultMessage: 'Out of stock',
102	            id: 'use_product.message.out_of_stock'
103	        }),
104	        [UNFULFILLABLE]: currentLowestStockLevelProductName
105	            ? intl.formatMessage(
106	                  {
107	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left for {productName}!',
108	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining_for_product'
109	                  },
110	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel, productName: currentLowestStockLevelProductName}
111	              )
112	            : intl.formatMessage(
113	                  {
114	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left!',
115	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining'
116	                  },
117	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel}
118	              )
119	    }
120	
121	    // showInventoryMessage controls if add to cart button is disabled
122	    const showInventoryMessage =
123	        (variant || isProductABundle || isStandardProduct) &&
124	        (currentIsOutOfStock || currentUnfulfillable)
125	    const inventoryMessage =
126	        (currentIsOutOfStock && inventoryMessages[OUT_OF_STOCK]) ||
127	        (currentUnfulfillable && inventoryMessages[UNFULFILLABLE])
128	
129	    // If the `initialQuantity` changes, update the state. This typically happens
130	    // when either the master product changes, or the inventory of the product changes
131	    // from out-of-stock to in-stock or vice versa.
132	    useEffect(() => {
133	        setQuantity(initialQuantity)
134	    }, [initialQuantity])
135	
136	    // Lump the out of stock/unfulfillable checks together for easier consumption
137	    return {
138	        showLoading,
139	        showInventoryMessage,
140	        inventoryMessage,
141	        variationAttributes,
142	        quantity,
143	        minOrderQuantity,
144	        stepQuantity,
145	        variationParams,
146	        setQuantity,
147	        variant,
148	        stockLevel,
149	        isOutOfStock,
150	        unfulfillable,
151	        isSelectedStoreOutOfStock: isSelectedStoreOutOfStock || selectedStoreUnfulfillable,
152	        selectedStore
153	    }
154	}

1	/**
2	 * Commerce/ProductView — Storybook stories for the ProductView override.
3	 *
4	 * Providers supplied by .storybook/preview.tsx: IntlProvider, ChakraProvider.
5	 * This file adds a MemoryRouter decorator to satisfy `useLocation`, and a minimal
6	 * inert provider stack to satisfy the hooks ProductView calls internally:
7	 *   ServerContext.Provider value={{}} — useSFPayments → useServerContext (no server request
8	 *     in Storybook; {} signals browser mode, same pattern as header/index.stories.tsx)
9	 *   MultiSiteProvider — StoreLocatorProvider → useMultiSite (reads site.id for localStorage key)
10	 *   CommerceApiProvider + QueryClientProvider — useShopperBasketsV2Mutation, useSFPayments,
11	 *     useExpressCheckoutEnabled, useCleanupTemporaryBaskets
12	 *   CurrencyProvider — useCurrency (reads CurrencyContext, separate from CommerceApiProvider)
13	 *   StoreLocatorProvider — useSelectedStore (reads selected store state)
14	 *   AddToCartModalProvider — useAddToCartModalContext (reads its own context)
15	 * `disableAuthInit` skips the token-init side-effect; placeholder config values and
16	 * an `.invalid` proxy URL prevent any real network calls. See rightBar/index.stories.tsx
17	 * for the full rationale on this provider pattern.
18	 */
19	import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
20	import { expect, fn, userEvent, within } from 'storybook/test';
21	import React from 'react';
22	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
23	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
24	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
25	import { CurrencyProvider, MultiSiteProvider, StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
26	import { AddToCartModalProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal';
27	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
28	import ProductView from '.';
29	
30	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	// Commerce provider stack (inert — no real API calls)
32	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	
34	// See rightBar/index.stories.tsx for the full rationale on why ProductView needs
35	// these providers and why this configuration is safe (disableAuthInit + .invalid proxy).
36	const storybookQueryClient = new QueryClient({
37	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
38	});
39	
40	// Inert store-locator config — no real BOPIS API calls in Storybook.
41	const STORYBOOK_STORE_LOCATOR_CONFIG = {
42	  radius: 100,
43	  radiusUnit: 'km',
44	  defaultCountry: 'AU',
45	  defaultCountryCode: 'AU',
46	  defaultPostalCode: '2000',
47	  defaultPageSize: 10,
48	  supportedCountries: [{ countryCode: 'AU', label: 'Australia', postalCodeRequired: true }],
49	};
50	
51	const CommerceProviders = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
52	  <QueryClientProvider client={storybookQueryClient}>
53	    <CommerceApiProvider
54	      clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
55	      organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
56	      shortCode="storybook"
57	      siteId="ZimmermannAU"
58	      locale="en-AU"
59	      currency="AUD"
60	      proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
61	      redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
62	      disableAuthInit
63	      silenceWarnings
64	    >
65	      {/* useCurrency reads from CurrencyContext; useAddToCartModalContext reads from
66	          AddToCartModalContext; useSelectedStore reads from StoreLocatorContext —
67	          none of these are covered by CommerceApiProvider. */}
68	      <CurrencyProvider currency="AUD">
69	        <StoreLocatorProvider config={STORYBOOK_STORE_LOCATOR_CONFIG}>
70	          <AddToCartModalProvider>{children}</AddToCartModalProvider>
71	        </StoreLocatorProvider>
72	      </CurrencyProvider>
73	    </CommerceApiProvider>
74	  </QueryClientProvider>
75	);

8	import {useCallback, useContext} from 'react'
9	import {MultiSiteContext} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts'
10	
11	/**
12	 * Custom React hook to get the function that returns usefule multi-site values, the site, the locale and
13	 * the function used to build URLs following the App configuration.
14	 * @returns {{site, locale, buildUrl: (function(*, *, *): *)}}
15	 */
16	const useMultiSite = () => {
17	    const context = useContext(MultiSiteContext)
18	    if (context === undefined) {
19	        throw new Error('useMultiSite must be used within MultiSiteProvider')
20	    }
21	    const {buildUrl: originalFn, site, locale} = context
22	
23	    const buildUrl = useCallback(
24	        (path, siteRef, localeRef) => {
25	            return originalFn(
26	                path,
27	                siteRef ? siteRef : site?.alias || site?.id,
28	                localeRef ? localeRef : locale?.alias || locale?.id
29	            )
30	        },
31	        [originalFn, site, locale]
32	    )
33	    return {site, locale, buildUrl}
34	}
35	
36	export default useMultiSite
37

input.message:
SFCC-270 commit 5 done, with one deliberate gap: gift-card suppression is NOT implemented — no real signal exists yet, explained below. Everything else is done and green.

## What breaks if this ships as-is
Nothing regresses — `order-summary`'s base `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` still overrides correctly (verified, not assumed — see mechanism below), and the item-name colour bug is fixed. The one gap: a digital gift-card cart line still shows a quantity stepper and actions row, same as today. Not a regression — commit 4 didn't suppress it either — just a spec item this commit couldn't safely build.

## Why: the gift-card signal doesn't exist yet
I searched this codebase and the commerce SDK for how a digital gift card line item is actually identified. Found one candidate — `GiftCertificateItem` in `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` (`amount`, `recipientEmail`, `recipientName`, no `productId`/`variationValues`) — but it lives in `basket.giftCertificateItems`, a wholly separate array from `basket.productItems`, and confirmed via `grep` that base retail-react-app never renders it through `ProductItem` at all. Using it here would be inventing a heuristic on a shape this component isn't built to receive. `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` schedules "Credit Notes & Gift Cards (GiveX)" for Sprint 6, later than current work, and zero gift-card code exists anywhere in `overrides/` today. Per the brief's own instruction ("stop and report rather than invent a heuristic"), I left `product-item/index.tsx`'s stepper/actions logic untouched and did not fabricate a `GiftCard` story that would falsely claim this behaviour — same reasoning `zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx`'s own docblock already uses for skipping a story it can't honestly back.

## Files changed
**Modified:** `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/{item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}.tsx`, `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (Tier 2 — registering the two new recipes, pre-authorized per this step's brief, stated not paused).
**Created:** `overrides/app/components/product-item/product-item.css.ts` (`ZimmCartItem`), `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-variant.css.ts` (`ZimmCartItemVariant`), `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.{test,stories}.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/index.test.tsx`. Nothing outside this list touched (`git status --short` confirms exactly these 11 files).

## Recipe parts, and why
`ZimmCartItem` (product-item.css.ts): `row` (image+details, gap 28px desktop/24px mobile via `--zimm-scale-700`/`--zimm-scale-xl`, align centre/start), `details` (gap 12px desktop/24px mobile via `--zimm-scale-s`/`--zimm-scale-xl`), `info` (name+colour-size+mobile-price block: column desktop / row+space-between mobile — mobile values match the pre-existing unconditional layout exactly, so nothing changes below `md`, only desktop is new).
`ZimmCartItemVariant` (item-variant.css.ts): `image` (responsive width 67px/132px, ivory-200 bg), `img` (objectFit contain/cover, mix-blend-multiply), `colourSize` (textStyle caption + regular-weight override + 200px width + secondary colour), `price` (textStyle price only).

**Non-obvious but load-bearing decision:** I verified by reading the compiled `@chakra-ui/system`/`@chakra-ui/layout` source (not assumed) that `__css` and `sx` are NOT interchangeable here. `toCSSObject` merges `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — `__css` is lowest priority, `sx` is highest. Worse: Chakra's own `Text` places its OWN `__css` key *after* `...rest` in its render call, so a caller-supplied `__css` on a plain `<Text>` is silently discarded entirely, not merged. So: `item-image.tsx`'s Box uses `__css` (must stay overridable by a caller's literal `width`/`mr` — proven, not assumed, by reading `Box`'s own empty-baseStyle source). Everything going onto a `<Text>`/`<Stack>`/`<Flex>` that doesn't need caller-override (`colourSize`, `price`, `row`, `details`, `info`) uses `sx`. Getting this backwards would have silently broken either the order-summary override contract or discarded the recipe styling entirely with no compile error — documented inline in both `.css.ts` files' docblocks with exact file citations. This isn't written down anywhere in `overrideStyling.md` today; worth turning into a documented rule since any future copy-first Chakra restyle will hit it again.

## Pass criteria — evidence
1. **product-item/index.test.tsx** (1 test, passing): image alt, uppercase name (asserted on the `<Heading>` `textStyle` is applied to — `text-transform` is CSS-inherited, and jsdom's `getComputedStyle` doesn't reliably resolve inherited values from a descendant, confirmed by first getting this wrong and seeing it fail), price renders, `getByText('Lilac Sand, One size')` proves ONE node holds both values (an exact-string query can't match a value split across two elements).
2. **item-variant/index.test.tsx**, width test: `toHaveStyle({width:'321px'})` passes with a caller-supplied width. **PASS.**
3. Same file, `mr` test: `toHaveStyle({marginRight:'37px'})` passes. **PASS.**
4. **NOT MET** — see above.
5. `recipeGuards.test.ts`: 6/6 pass (full suite run). Keys are exactly `ZimmCartItem`/`ZimmCartItemVariant`, `Zimm*`-namespaced; zero bare token keys (all `var(--zimm-*)`).
6. `recipeParts.test.ts`: 41/41 pass. Caveat I found and want on record: this guard's sibling-matching is literally `index.tsx`-named — `item-variant.css.ts`'s real consumers (`item-image.tsx`, `item-attributes.tsx`, `item-price.tsx`) aren't named `index.tsx`, so this guard passes *vacuously* for that recipe (nothing it reads counts as "declared but unread"). I manually verified every declared part is genuinely read, but the automated check doesn't actually cover it — matches that test's own documented "out of reach" caveat, just a fresh instance of it.
7. `npm run audit:tokens`: unacknowledged violations went **10 → 7** repo-wide. In product-item/item-variant scope specifically: baseline 7 (`84px`, `88px`, `136px` — all removed) → now 4, all four pre-existing and untouched (image badges' `10px`×2, `PricePerItem`'s `12px`/`14px`). 3 new entries (`67px`, `132px`, `200px`) landed as **acknowledged exceptions** (audit-allow comments), not violations. Net: reduced, not held flat, not added to.
8. `grep -n "\[" product-item/index.tsx` → 3 hits, none the tested pattern: a `[overrides]` string inside a comment, `display={[...]}` inside my own prose comment (not code), and `any[]` (a TS array type annotation). Zero actual Chakra responsive-array shorthand remains.
9. Stories exist at `Commerce/ProductItem`: `Default`, `MultipleItems`. **`GiftCard` deliberately omitted** — see above.
10. Verified by code review (not by an automated 402px check — see below): no `noOfLines`, `isTruncated`, `text-overflow`, or `display:none` was added anywhere on name/price/colourSize/stepper/actions.

**Criterion 10's real constraint, disclosed not glossed over:** this repo has no Storybook viewport addon configured, `.storybook/` is Tier 1 (can't add one), and `npm run test` (Vitest) never executes `.stories.tsx` files at all (not in `vitest.config.ts`'s `include`). `header/rightBar/index.test.tsx:128-129`'s own comment confirms jsdom doesn't evaluate CSS media queries at all. So a genuine "at 402px, nothing is clipped" check isn't mechanically provable by anything this repo's harness currently runs — I did the honest version (code-level absence of any truncation CSS) rather than write a play function whose assertion would look real but prove nothing.

## Judgment calls I made and am flagging (not hidden in a comment, said here)
- **"Item Info" scope**: I mapped it to the existing name+attrs+mobile-price / desktop-delivery-actions Flex (column desktop/row mobile), reusing the existing element rather than restructuring. No pass criterion tests this specific grouping either way — flagged as my best-conservative read of the Figma record, not a guess on a tested value.
- **primaryAction breakpoint**: base file split the mobile/desktop primaryAction slots at Chakra's default `sm` (480px, via responsive arrays); I unified both to this file's own already-established `md` (768px) `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` split (required anyway to kill the array shorthand for criterion 8) since no Figma value distinguishes it and the rest of this exact file already uses 768px.
- **Item image aspect ratio**: Figma gives both "288/432" and "67×100 mobile" — these don't perfectly agree (67×1.5=100.5, not 100). Used the ratio as the single source of truth (matches the 132×198 desktop pair exactly); mobile lands at 100.5px, a documented half-pixel rounding gap, same class of issue `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own `WIDTH_XLARGE` note already discloses for a different value.

## Full command output
`npx tsc --noEmit` → clean, exit 0.
`npm run test` → **85 test files, 1238 tests, all passing** (includes `recipeGuards.test.ts` and `recipeParts.test.ts`).
`npm run audit:tokens` → 7 unacknowledged (down from 10 baseline before this commit).

## What Marcel is missing
This isn't a one-off gap in commit 5 — gift-card handling is going to recur across the rest of this 18-commit Cart plan (mini-cart, cart-page actions, checkout gating are all in the GC PRD), and right now there's no discoverable answer anywhere in this codebase for "how does SFCC actually represent one of these line items" — worth resolving that once (with backend/SI), rather than hitting this same stop-and-report at 3-4 more commits downstream.

## Recipe parts, and why
`ZimmCartItem` (product-item.css.ts): `row` (image+details, gap 28px desktop/24px mobile via `--zimm-scale-700`/`--zimm-scale-xl`, align centre/start), `details` (gap 12px desktop/24px mobile via `--zimm-scale-s`/`--zimm-scale-xl`), `info` (name+colour-size+mobile-price block: column desktop / row+space-between mobile — mobile values match the pre-existing unconditional layout exactly, so nothing changes below `md`, only desktop is new).
`ZimmCartItemVariant` (item-variant.css.ts): `image` (responsive width 67px/132px, ivory-200 bg), `img` (objectFit contain/cover, mix-blend-multiply), `colourSize` (textStyle caption + regular-weight override + 200px width + secondary colour), `price` (textStyle price only).

**Non-obvious but load-bearing decision:** I verified by reading the compiled `@chakra-ui/system`/`@chakra-ui/layout` source (not assumed) that `__css` and `sx` are NOT interchangeable here. `toCSSObject` merges `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — `__css` is lowest priority, `sx` is highest. Worse: Chakra's own `Text` places its OWN `__css` key *after* `...rest` in its render call, so a caller-supplied `__css` on a plain `<Text>` is silently discarded entirely, not merged. So: `item-image.tsx`'s Box uses `__css` (must stay overridable by a caller's literal `width`/`mr` — proven, not assumed, by reading `Box`'s own empty-baseStyle source). Everything going onto a `<Text>`/`<Stack>`/`<Flex>` that doesn't need caller-override (`colourSize`, `price`, `row`, `details`, `info`) uses `sx`. Getting this backwards would have silently broken either the order-summary override contract or discarded the recipe styling entirely with no compile error — documented inline in both `.css.ts` files' docblocks with exact file citations. This isn't written down anywhere in `overrideStyling.md` today; worth turning into a documented rule since any future copy-first Chakra restyle will hit it again.

## Judgment calls I made and am flagging (not hidden in a comment, said here)
- **"Item Info" scope**: I mapped it to the existing name+attrs+mobile-price / desktop-delivery-actions Flex (column desktop/row mobile), reusing the existing element rather than restructuring. No pass criterion tests this specific grouping either way — flagged as my best-conservative read of the Figma record, not a guess on a tested value.
- **primaryAction breakpoint**: base file split the mobile/desktop primaryAction slots at Chakra's default `sm` (480px, via responsive arrays); I unified both to this file's own already-established `md` (768px) `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` split (required anyway to kill the array shorthand for criterion 8) since no Figma value distinguishes it and the rest of this exact file already uses 768px.
